decision: ADR-020 §3: minimal Action/queue authority for NexLoop's own service principals, applied by the scheduler through trusted configuration (0050) only. v2: claim_matcher follows successor versions of Consumer.edit published by human review decisions (follow_latest_version). v3: claim_matcher per-object Consumer property READ/EDIT derived from a type rule (property_access_rules, docs/implementation/property-grant-derivation.md); restricted groups come only from the separate owner file deploy/authorization/owner-property-restrictions.json. v4: background feeds (0092) — recall_indexer drains recall-instance, claim_matcher drains claim-match (feed authority only; indexing/matching/writes keep their own checks). v5: deployment plan B (0099) — message_read_rules bind Message/Conversation READ to the work itself: the extraction worker reads only the Conversation and Messages of an extraction task its credential currently leases; the matcher reads only the evidence Message and Conversation of a Claim still to be matched. Derived in SQL at each use; rule or Action revocation, Message deletion, leaving the Conversation, task completion or Claim resolution end it. v6: nexloop.context.assemble:1 is issued with each Run (0104): the Source carries the Run credential it issued for that Run, valid only while the Run is active and for that Run's own pack; the standing context_assembler principal is retired and its grants are revoked on apply. v7: NX-024 plan reevaluation — plan_reevaluator drains plan-reevaluate and runs the deterministic precheck (nexloop.plan.reevaluate); runtime_worker records run-outcomes of reevaluation Runs (nexloop.plan.outcome), bound in SQL to the live activation and its own task lease. v8: ADR-023 reply guarantee — reply_guarantor drains reply-due (pending replies registered in the inbound Message's own transaction, 0109), reads the state of one pending reply, starts its fallback reply Run or escalates it to the owner with evidence (nexloop.reply.guarantee), and reads contact restrictions and escalations (nexloop.contact.read). It cannot write, lift or weaken a contact restriction. v9: ADR-023 fallback reply Run (0110) — message_relay also issues the one fallback reply Run of an unanswered inbound message (nexloop.reply.fallback), with the same MessageAssignment checks as the original message Run; SQL refuses a second one and refuses it once the message is settled. v10: NX-026 commitments — commitment_keeper drains commitment-register (commitment Claims marked in their own transaction) and commitment-monitor (evidence, human requests, restrictions, due stages), prepares registrations and evaluates transitions in SQL (nexloop.commitment.keep), creates Commitment objects with exactly the prepared properties (Commitment.create) and applies only ledger-derived transitions (Commitment.edit) under a per-object EDIT derived only for the commitment_lifecycle group; it reads commitments and exceptions (nexloop.commitment.read). It writes no evidence of its own and holds no human commitment Action. v11: NX-027 commercial events — commercial_recorder drains commercial-record (records marked by verified signed events, refunds and link changes in their own transaction), derives the record state in SQL (nexloop.commercial.record), creates and edits CommercialRecord objects only with that state (CommercialRecord.create / CommercialRecord.edit, per-object EDIT derived only for the commercial_state group) and reads records (nexloop.commercial.read) and cost entries and settlements (nexloop.cost.read). It holds no human Action, cannot configure connectors and never sees connector keys. v12: NX-028 D3 — reply_guarantor also drains takeover-expiry and ends an expired human takeover (nexloop.takeover.expire: D5 settlement, hand-back control event, owner escalation); it cannot start, extend or hand back a takeover (human Actions only). v13: NX-029 slice 1 — retention_keeper runs the retention sweeps through nexloop.retention.execute (0141): it asks which classes are due and runs bounded passes; SQL decides what expires, opens append-only rows only inside its own sweep transaction and leaves tombstones without content. The keeper holds no table privilege, never sees content and holds no human Action. v14: NX-029 slice 2 — retention_keeper also drives confirmed Consumer erasures, purges settled Run directories through the Agent Host loopback and deletes expired or erased Artifacts of any principal through the owner-internal port nexloop.erasure.execute (0142); SQL re-verifies every id, a tombstone and an audit event follow only a confirmed deletion.

principals.purpose: Debounce accepted conversations and enqueue one idempotent extraction window per conversation.
Claim extraction tasks from the durable queue and record Claims through the governed extraction function.
Four-layer Claim matching and the governed formal write of accepted matches.
Re-derive or remove instance recall index rows for objects marked in the recall-instance feed; holds no business READ/EDIT (recall filters by the reader's own READ).
Lease due plans, run the deterministic precheck and link one bounded reevaluation Run; writes only plan working state, never business facts.
Drain due pending replies; start the fallback reply Run for an unanswered inbound message or escalate it to the owner with evidence. Never sends on its own and never touches contact restrictions.
Lease Run activation tasks from the operations queue and hand them to the Agent Host guard.
Materialize a channel-accepted Agent reply as a Message through the governed Message.agent_create Action; never sends, never chooses text or delivery state.
Route an accepted inbound Message to a Run activation event.
Register enterprise commitments from delivered commitment Claims and move their status only on ledger evidence; marks plans at due stages and raises owner-visible exceptions.
Turn verified signed commercial events into CommercialRecord objects with exactly the state SQL derives (corrections, late events, refunds, customer links); never from a customer's statement.

Run the tenant's retention sweeps through the signed retention port: redact expired message text, Claim quotes, prompt text and job inputs, delete expired receipts, observations, financial records and cost entries, leaving tombstones without content.

Establish plans, precheck them against current controls and facts, mark them invalid/closed and link reevaluation Runs.
Lease pending replies registered in the inbound Message's own transaction (0109).
Read the state of one pending reply; start its fallback reply Run or escalate it with evidence (0109).
Read contact restrictions and reply escalations (query port before NX-028).
Lease human takeovers when they reach expires_at (0152).
End an expired takeover: D5 settlement, hand-back control event, owner escalation (0152).
Record a reevaluation Run's run-outcome from its Host; SQL binds it to the live activation under this worker's own task lease.
Claim/renew/finish Run activation tasks (queue name as deployed by the message recipe).
Issue the one fallback reply Run of an inbound message still unanswered when its fallback time comes (ADR-023 §2.7, 0110).
Route an accepted inbound Message into a Run activation.
Governed creation of the Message object for an outbound reply already accepted by the channel (ADR-020 §2).
Lease commitment Claims marked in the same transaction that recorded them (0111).
Lease commitments marked by evidence, human requests, contact restrictions and due stages (0111).
Prepare registrations from the Claim and its delivered outbound Message, record them, evaluate and settle ledger-derived transitions (0111).
Read commitments with their evidence columns and exceptions (query port before NX-028).
Governed creation of a Commitment with exactly the prepared properties (SQL guard, 0111).
Governed status transition derived from the evidence ledger (SQL guard, 0111); per-object EDIT comes from the commitment_lifecycle rule.
Type-level READ carried by the derived per-object Commitment EDIT proofs.
Lease records marked by verified events, refunds and link changes in their own transaction (0130).
Prepare the derived record state and record it (event dispositions, downstream hook) (0130).
Read records, their events and exceptions, and receipt counts (query port before NX-028).
Read cost entries per kind and currency and budget settlements (query port before NX-028; 0132).
Governed creation of a CommercialRecord with exactly the derived state (SQL guard, 0130).
Governed application of the derived state (SQL guard, 0130); per-object EDIT comes from the commercial_state rule.
Type-level READ carried by the derived per-object CommercialRecord EDIT proofs.
Ask which retention classes are due and run bounded sweep passes; SQL decides what expires and holds every table privilege (0141).

deferred.reason: Real outbound effect execution; channel enablement and REAL_DISPATCH_ENABLED need the owner's own confirmation (ADR-020 §3).
Provider query of real outbound effects; enabled together with the channel by the owner.
Receipt reconciliation of real outbound effects; enabled together with the channel by the owner.
Never a static per-Message grant: Source READ is derived from governed facts (ADR-020 §1, NX-047); extraction worker and matcher READ is derived per purpose from message_read_rules (v5, 0099).
Per-object authority of the matcher depends on instance data; needs governed derivation, not a static manifest.
Held by Run-bound Source credentials issued per Run (0034), not by a standing service principal.

Issued with each Run (0104): the Source presents the Run credential it issued, accepted only while that Run is active, unexpired and not ended, and for a v6 bind only for that Run's own pack; never a standing service grant (former context_assembler, retired in v6).
Planning authority belongs to Agent/Run credentials (NX-022/NX-024), not service principals.
Owner control configuration; human owner authority.
Browser human identity link flow; human authority.
Recorded by the Run Source path of an outbound request; follows the effect channel decision.

property_access_rules.purpose: Apply accepted Claims to every real-world Consumer without per-object grants; all ten ADR-019 §2 groups (owner decision 2026-10-09: none restricted); groups restricted by the owner are never derived.

Edit only the lifecycle properties (status, late, fulfillment_basis, fulfillment_evidence) of every real-world Commitment; content properties are outside the rule and the SQL guard accepts only ledger-derived transitions.
Edit only the state properties of every CommercialRecord of its world; identity properties are outside the rule and the SQL guard accepts only the state derived from verified events.

message_read_rules.purpose: Read the window of the extraction task it currently leases: that Conversation (object, consumer_id, owner_principal) and the task's Messages; nothing outside the leased task.
Read the Claims of a Conversation (Conversation object) and the evidence Message of a Claim still to be matched; ends when the Claim is resolved.

retired_principals.reason: nexloop.context.assemble:1 is issued with each Run (0104); no caller uses a standing assembler credential.

excluded_by_policy: Human principal authority of any kind
